name: Grade 2 — Science
subject: science
description: Plants, animals, senses, and our world

questions.question: What do plants need to make their own food?
questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide (air) to make food through photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which part of a plant soaks up water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and minerals from the soil.

questions.question: {{userName}} touches a hot cup and quickly pulls away. Which sense helped?
questions.explanation: The sense of touch (skin) detects heat and pain, helping {{userName}} react quickly.

questions.question: How many sense organs does a human body have?
questions.explanation: Humans have 5 sense organs: eyes (sight), ears (hearing), nose (smell), tongue (taste), and skin (touch).

questions.question: What do caterpillars turn into?
questions.explanation: A caterpillar forms a chrysalis and transforms (metamorphosis) into a butterfly.

questions.question: Which animal gives us milk?
questions.explanation: Cows are domestic animals that give us milk. Buffalo and goats also give milk.

questions.question: What gives us light and warmth during the day?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star that provides light and heat energy to Earth.

questions.question: {{userName}} plants a seed in wet soil and puts it near a window. What two things will help it grow?
questions.explanation: Seeds need water to germinate and sunlight to grow into a healthy plant.

questions.question: Animals that eat only plants are called?
questions.explanation: Herbivores eat only plants. Examples: cow, deer, rabbit.

questions.question: What season has the most rain?
questions.explanation: Monsoon (rainy season) brings heavy rainfall. In India, monsoon occurs from June to September.

questions.question: Which of these is a living thing?
questions.explanation: A tree is a living organism — it grows, breathes, and reproduces. Rocks, chairs, and books are non-living.

questions.question: We breathe in which gas to stay alive?
questions.explanation: Humans breathe in oxygen (O₂) and breathe out carbon dioxide (CO₂).
